No Result View All Result Home News Politics Business Sport Football Health Entertainment Education Opinion Editorial Columns Others LeVogue Magazine Conferences National Economy Contact Us Hausa Edition Home News Politics Business Sport Football Health Entertainment Education Opinion Editorial Columns Others LeVogue Magazine Conferences National Economy Contact Us No Result View All Result No Result View All Result I Hoped Fasoranti Would Witness My 2nd Term — Tinubu by Jonathan Nda-Isaiah 7 seconds ago in News Share on WhatsApp Share on Facebook Share on X Telegram President Bola Tinubu has expressed sadness over the death of foremost Afenifere leader, Pa Reuben Famuyide Fasoranti, saying he had hoped the centenarian would live to witness his second term in office and the anticipated economic growth and prosperity of Nigeria.
Tinubu, who described Fasoranti as a father, patriarch, elder statesman and one of the last great figures of the progressive political tradition associated with the late Chief Obafemi Awolowo, said the country had lost a man of immense wisdom and moral authority.
The President stated this in a condolence message personally signed by him on Tuesday following the death of the Afenifere leader at the age of 100.
He recalled his visit to Fasoranti’s residence in Akure in 2022, when he informed the elder statesman of his decision to contest the presidency.
According to Tinubu, Fasoranti prayed for him during the visit and expressed confidence that he would become President within his lifetime.
“I also recall his prayers and counsel when I came to his residence in Akure in 2022 to inform him of my decision to contest the presidency. Pa Fasoranti told me I would be President in his lifetime, and God answered his prayer,” he said.
The President added that he had hoped the late Afenifere leader would remain alive to witness his second term and the full realisation of economic growth and prosperity in the country.
“I had hoped Papa would also be around with us for my second term to witness the full dawn of economic growth and prosperity in the land,” Tinubu said.
Despite his grief, the President urged Nigerians to be thankful for Fasoranti’s long life of service, describing his century on earth as a period marked by grace, commitment and fulfilment.
Tinubu said the late elder statesman’s life exemplified integrity, discipline, selflessness and an unwavering commitment to the Yoruba people and the unity and progress of Nigeria.
He also paid tribute to Fasoranti’s contributions to democracy, noting that he fought for the democratic freedoms Nigerians enjoy today, even at the risk of his life.
From his career as an educationist and principal to his service as Commissioner for Finance in the old Ondo State and later as Afenifere leader, the President said Fasoranti remained committed to true federalism, social justice and a Nigeria that works for all.
Tinubu described him as an icon and a beacon of principle whose moral authority and fatherly counsel would be sorely missed, particularly at a time when the country needed his guidance.
He also extended condolences to the Fasoranti family, the people of Akure Kingdom, the Ondo State Government and people, South-West Nigeria and the entire Afenifere family.
The President prayed for the repose of the deceased’s soul and asked God to grant his family and all those mourning the loss the strength to bear the bereavement.
